name: Palpa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Glottolog Bookkeeping languoid; only refs are ISO 639-3 registration documents; no descriptive material exists.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2019. Change Request Number 2019-034: retire [plp] Palpa (adopted 2020-01-23). SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; administrative document. p.2: 2010 Nepal Audit 'There is no known attestation for Palpa as a separate language, or even dialect'; cites Nida 1972:345 ('Palpa is the form of Pahari spoken in western Nepal.. midway between Eastern Pahari (Nepali) and Central Pahari (Kumaoni)') and Hugoniot 1970 (Palpa listed as a dialect of Nepali); SIL linguist: 'safe enough to say that it is a dialect of Nepali'.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part IV: Indo-Aryan Family, Central Group: Specimens of the Pahari Languages and Gujuri. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. [Introduction p.18; Khas-kura 'Pronunciation' pp.22-23; 'Palpa Dialect' pp.75-80]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. Palpa note p.75: 'Pronunciation.--This is apparently much as in standard Khas-kura. In the word nisaki for nikasi, there has been a metathesis of s and k. In many words a final a is not sounded, thus approaching the pronunciation of Kumauni.' The Khas-kura (Nepali) Pronunciation section pp.22-23 treats vowel length, e/ya spellings and nasalization only; no accent/stress statement (a full-text search for stress/accent the whole Khas-kura section for accent/stress/emphasis: 0 relevant hits; the volume's accent remarks are all in the Western Pahari and Khowar-convention passages).
Nothing; confirms Bookkeeping status, ISO retirement 2019-034 'non-existent', AES 'extinct' per Simons & Fennig 2018; only descriptive-type ref is Grierson 1916.

sources.note: The only modern first-hand assessment of speech in the Palpa area; would confirm identity with Nepali (it is not expected to contain a stress statement). Internal SIL document, never published.
